findings.title: Compare-and-set relies on decode→encode reproducing the stored payload_json byte for byte
findings.body: The guard compares the stored `payload_json` string with `encodeProviderThreadPayload(expected)`, where `expected` is a row decoded by `getThreadRecords`. That matches only if re-encoding a decoded row gives exactly the text that was stored. `provider-thread.updated` stores `encodeProviderThreadPayload(event.payload)` (ProjectionStore.ts:2204), so rows written by the current schema should match. A row stored by an older build, with a field since dropped or a different key order or default, would decode and re-encode to different text. The guard then returns `committed: false` on every attempt. `writeReleasedBackgroundWorkEvents` retries 3 times, logs `provider-session-release-roster-conflict`, and leaves the roster in place, so the thread stays Waiting (#15239) with only a log line. Are persisted provider-thread rows guaranteed to round-trip byte-identically, including rows written before schema changes? If not, compare a canonical form, or the fields this write owns, instead of the whole string.

findings.title: New compare-and-set sink method has no direct persistence test
findings.body: The sibling guarded writes `writeIfRunCurrent` and `writeIfProviderThreadOwner` each have committed and rejected-case tests against the real sink in FoundationPersistence.test.ts (around lines 1582 to 1848). `writeIfProviderThreadUnchanged` is only reached through ProviderSessionManager tests, and its not-committed branch is exercised only once, via a wrapper that runs the hook before delegating. No test covers a missing row, or the exhausted-retries path that logs `provider-session-release-roster-conflict`. A test of the real sink would pin the whole-row comparison semantics the doc comment describes.

contracts.action: On session release (detach, idle, manual close), remove the dead process's pending background tasks from its provider threads' rosters via a compare-and-set write
contracts.equivalent_path: ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService clears every roster on startup/shutdown, and Orchestrator settleInterruptedRun clears rosters of provider threads with no live session. Both write whole-row `provider-thread.updated` events from a projection read earlier.
contracts.before_after: Before: a released session's roster stayed in the projection, so the thread showed Waiting until server restart (#15239). After: `releaseEntry` reads the roster right after removing the live entry (`readReleasedBackgroundTasks`), closes the scope, then `writeReleasedBackgroundWorkEvents` re-reads each provider thread, drops only the captured task ids, and commits through `writeIfProviderThreadUnchanged` (full-row JSON compare, up to 3 attempts). The recovery sibling also records cancelled work on the run and sets active threads idle. This path does neither: it clears only the roster and leaves status untouched. Server shutdown and runtimes without `backgroundTasksEndWithProcess` are skipped. Both exclusive adapters (Claude, Muse) report `supportsMultipleProviderThreadsPerSession: false`, so a detach releases on the last thread and `attachedThreadIds` plus `detachedThreadId` covers its threads.
contracts.visible_effect: The Waiting state clears after archive/detach/idle release for Claude and Muse threads. Replacement-session tasks and tasks owned by another session's provider threads are kept.
contracts.failure_mode: The read and the write are guarded: a concurrent update makes the write retry with fresh state, and read failures are logged and swallowed. After 3 conflicts, or if the stored JSON never equals the re-encoded row, the roster stays and only a warning is logged. The read happens after the entry leaves the live map, so a task the dying adapter reports in that window is not cleared. The write also runs inside `writeReleaseRecords`, which `retryReleaseRecords` re-runs on failure; the re-read makes it idempotent.

summary: The change clears the pending-background-task roster when a Claude or Muse session is released, using a new whole-row compare-and-set write. The logic holds up against the code I read: both adapters are exclusive-session, the capture happens right after the live entry is removed, and the write re-reads and retries. I found no blocker. Two lower-severity points remain. The compare-and-set assumes stored `payload_json` round-trips byte-identically through decode and encode, and a mismatch would leave the roster in place with only a warning. The new sink method also has no direct test in FoundationPersistence.test.ts, unlike its sibling guarded writes.
